# Clément Callaert

MSc, CentraleSupélec · M2 Mathematics and AI, Université Paris-Saclay\
Until September 2026: apprentice AI engineer, MBDA

[GitHub](https://github.com/clement-callaert) ·
[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/clement-callaert) ·
[CV](cv.qmd)

I work on generative models of dynamics: probability paths and flow matching,
latent world models for planning, and how these behave when the sampling
budget is small.

The projects below are personal work done on a single GPU, not lab research.
Each has a public repository, a short report, and an explicit note on what the
result does not show. I am applying for PhD positions starting in 2027.

## Projects

### Few-step field regularity

At a fixed number of function evaluations, lower averaged Jacobian regularity
does not reliably imply lower sampling error. 14 of 36 path comparisons in the
registered grid reverse the two orderings. Exact Gaussian systems only.

[code](https://github.com/clement-callaert/fewstep-field-regularity) ·
[manuscript](https://github.com/clement-callaert/fewstep-field-regularity/blob/main/paper/arxiv/main.pdf) ·
[audit](https://github.com/clement-callaert/fewstep-field-regularity/blob/main/audit/CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md)

### Ego-world JEPA

Strong latent decodability did not produce a planning benefit on PushT. The
seed-0 gap was not significant (p = 0.269) and did not replicate on seed 1.
Two seeds, one setup. Frozen.

[code](https://github.com/clement-callaert/ego-world-sub-jepa) ·
[results](https://github.com/clement-callaert/ego-world-sub-jepa/blob/main/results/manifest.json)

### Adaptive latent search

A learned stop-or-continue policy matched a gradient-norm rule but used more
steps. The oracle gap suggests the idea is not dead; this implementation of it
is.

[code](https://github.com/clement-callaert/lpn/tree/research/stochastic-latent-search) ·
[report](https://github.com/clement-callaert/lpn/blob/research/stochastic-latent-search/report/main.pdf)
